title: Where Are You Standing?
brief: First thing on shift: put your position on the record. Run `pwd` to print the full path of the directory you are standing in.
objective: Print the full path of the directory you are standing in.
successMessage: `pwd` prints the absolute path of where you are. That line is the first entry in tonight's log.

title: What Is In Here?
brief: Look around before you touch anything. Run `ls` to list the files and folders in the directory you are standing in.
objective: List the files and folders in the directory you are standing in.
successMessage: Three directories and a `welcome.txt` the day crew left open for you. Read it whenever you like.

title: Reveal Hidden Dotfiles
brief: On Linux a filename that begins with a dot is hidden from a plain listing, and the observer before you left something in your home directory with exactly that kind of name. Use `ls -la` to list everything, hidden files included.
objective: List everything in your home directory, hidden files included.
successMessage: `-a` shows the hidden entries — `.bashrc`, `.profile`, and a `.handover` nobody mentioned. `-l` adds permissions and sizes.

title: Changing Directories
brief: Tonight's paperwork lives in `Documents`. Run `cd Documents` to move into it.
objective: Move into the `Documents` directory.
successMessage: You are now working inside `/home/student/Documents`. The prompt follows you.

title: Climbing Up (..)
brief: The symbol `..` always means the parent directory. From `Documents`, run `cd ..` to get back to your home directory.
objective: Move from `Documents` back up to your home directory.
successMessage: `..` is relative to wherever you are, so it works from any directory on the machine.

title: Read the Night Notes
brief: Print the whole of `Documents/notes.txt` with `cat` and find out what tonight's target is.
objective: Print the whole of `Documents/notes.txt` on screen.

success.text:
Dome Status: sealed
Tonight Target: NGC 7331
Night Lead: student

successMessage: NGC 7331 it is. `cat` reads a file straight through and prints it to the screen.

title: First Few Lines (head)
brief: `Documents/data.csv` is the duty roster. Show only its first 3 lines with `head` — the column names, and the first two people on it.
objective: Show only the first 3 lines of `Documents/data.csv`.
successMessage: `head -n N` stops after N lines, which is how you look at a huge file without drowning in it.

title: Last Few Lines (tail)
brief: Show only the last 2 lines of `Documents/data.csv` with `tail`.
objective: Show only the last 2 lines of `Documents/data.csv`.
successMessage: `tail` is where you look first in a log file, because the newest lines are at the bottom.

title: Wildcard Globbing (*)
brief: The observatory website lives in `projects/web`. List every `.js` file in there with a single `*` pattern instead of typing filenames: `ls projects/web/*.js`.
objective: List every `.js` file in `projects/web` with a single wildcard pattern.
successMessage: The shell expanded `*.js` into the matching filenames before `ls` ever ran. The command never saw the star.

title: Multiple Wildcards
brief: List every `.txt` file in `Documents` with one wildcard pattern.
objective: List every `.txt` file in `Documents` with a single wildcard pattern.
successMessage: Two files matched and the roster and the access log did not. A pattern is faster than a list, and it never goes stale.

title: BOSS: The Handover Note
brief: The observer before you left a note in your home directory, and a plain listing will not show it. Find it, read it, and submit the dome key written inside — it was generated for you alone, so nobody else can hand it to you.
objective: Find the hidden note in your home directory, read it, and submit the dome key inside.

hints.text: A hidden filename starts with a dot, and one `ls` find lists those too. Once you can see the name, print the file.
The file is `.handover`. Read it with `cat`, then paste the FIND{...} value into the box.

successMessage: Hidden files are hidden by convention, not by security. Listing them is the first thing to do on an unfamiliar machine — and that key was yours alone.

title: Search Patterns with grep
brief: Pull every line out of `Documents/data.csv` that mentions the word `active`. `grep` is the tool that prints the lines matching a pattern.
objective: Print every line of `Documents/data.csv` that mentions `active`.

success.text:
101,Alice Reyes,Optics,95,active
102,Bo Nakamura,Records,82,active
103,Chidi Adeyemi,Optics,105,active
104,Dana Ilves,Weather,115,active
105,Evan Wright,Outreach,78,inactive
106,Fiona Marsh,Weather,120,active

hints.text: `grep` wants the pattern first and the file second.

successMessage: All six came back — because `inactive` contains `active`. grep matches anywhere in the line, not whole words.

title: Case-Insensitive Grep (-i)
brief: The dome controller writes `logs/app_errors.log`, and it spells trouble three different ways: ERROR, Error and error. Find all three of them in one search.
objective: Find every error line in `logs/app_errors.log` in one search, whatever its capitalisation.

predicates.text:
[2026-08-17 01:15:20] ERROR: Connection refused to weather feed on port 5432
[2026-08-17 02:40:11] Error: Shutter position sensor returned no reading
[2026-08-17 03:10:00] error: Disk quota warning on partition /var

hints.text: One short `grep` find makes the match ignore letter case.

successMessage: Three lines, three capitalisations. Case sensitivity is the commonest reason a search "finds nothing" when the thing is right there.

title: Inverting Matches (-v)
brief: `logs/app_errors.log` is mostly INFO noise. Show every line EXCEPT the ones containing INFO.
objective: Print every line of `logs/app_errors.log` except the ones containing `INFO`.

predicates.text:
[2026-08-17 01:15:20] ERROR: Connection refused to weather feed on port 5432
[2026-08-17 01:15:25] WARN: Retrying connection in 5 seconds
[2026-08-17 02:40:11] Error: Shutter position sensor returned no reading
[2026-08-17 03:10:00] error: Disk quota warning on partition /var

hints.text: One `grep` find inverts the match, so it prints the lines that do NOT match.

successMessage: Removing what you already understand is often faster than describing what you are looking for.

title: Line Counting (wc -l)
brief: How many requests did the observatory website serve last night? Count the lines in `Documents/server_access.log`.
objective: Count the lines in `Documents/server_access.log`.

hints.text: `wc` counts lines, words and bytes. One find limits it to lines.

successMessage: Ten requests. `wc -l` counts newlines, which is why a file with no final newline can read one short.

title: Sorting Numbers (sort -n)
brief: `Documents/dome_temps.log` is one dome temperature reading per line, in the order the controller logged them. Put them in order, coldest first. `sort` reads text by default, and a two-digit reading can land in the wrong place unless it is told the column holds numbers.
objective: Sort the readings in `Documents/dome_temps.log` from lowest to highest.

hints.text: `sort` compares lines as text by default. One find tells it to compare them as numbers instead.

successMessage: Without the numeric find, 12 sorts before 9, because alphabetically "1" comes before "9".

title: Sorting by Field (sort -t / -k)
brief: `Documents/data.csv` is comma separated, and column 4 is the hours each person logged. Put the roster in order by that column, smallest number first. You already know the find that keeps it numeric; `sort` also needs to be told the separator and which column to use.
objective: Put `Documents/data.csv` in order by column 4, smallest number first.

predicates.text:
id,name,team,hours,status
105,Evan Wright,Outreach,78,inactive
102,Bo Nakamura,Records,82,active
101,Alice Reyes,Optics,95,active
103,Chidi Adeyemi,Optics,105,active
104,Dana Ilves,Weather,115,active
106,Fiona Marsh,Weather,120,active

hints.text: Two more finds: one sets the field separator, one picks the field number. Comma is the separator here, and hours is the fourth field.

successMessage: Same numeric find as before, now aimed at one column of a bigger file instead of the whole line.

title: Field Extraction (cut)
brief: From `Documents/data.csv`, print only column 2 (the name) and column 4 (the hours). `cut` slices columns out of delimited text.
objective: Print only column 2 and column 4 of `Documents/data.csv`.

predicates.text:
name,hours
Alice Reyes,95
Bo Nakamura,82
Chidi Adeyemi,105
Dana Ilves,115
Evan Wright,78
Fiona Marsh,120

hints.text: One find sets the delimiter, another picks the fields. Separate the two field numbers with a comma and no space.

successMessage: Two columns out of five. This is how you hand a colleague the part of a file they asked for and nothing else.

title: The Pipeline (grep | wc -l)
brief: How many requests in `Documents/server_access.log` came back with status 401? Do it in one line: find the matching lines, then feed them straight into a counter.
objective: Print, in one line, how many requests in `Documents/server_access.log` returned status 401.

hints.text: The `|` operator sends one command's output into the next one as its input.

successMessage: Two rejected logins. Any command that reads that log and prints 2 is accepted here — `grep -c` does it without a pipe at all.

title: Output Redirection (>)
brief: Save every error line from `logs/app_errors.log` — all three spellings — into a new file at `/tmp/critical_errors.txt`. Nothing should appear on the screen.
objective: Save every error line from `logs/app_errors.log` into `/tmp/critical_errors.txt`, with nothing on screen.

hints.text: `>` sends a command's output into a file instead of the screen.

successMessage: The screen stayed empty because the output went to the file instead. `>` creates the file, or empties it first if it already existed.

title: Append Redirection (>>)
brief: Add the line `Audit log verified` to the END of `/tmp/audit_trail.log` without erasing anything already in it.
objective: Add the line `Audit log verified` to the end of `/tmp/audit_trail.log` without erasing what is already there.

hints.text: `>` overwrites. Doubling that same operator appends instead. `echo` produces the text to append.

successMessage: One character is the difference between adding a line to a log and destroying the log. This is worth remembering before you type `>`.

title: Split Output (tee)
brief: Show every `Weather` line from `Documents/data.csv` on screen AND save those same lines to `/tmp/weather_team.txt`, in one command.
objective: Show every `Weather` line from `Documents/data.csv` on screen AND save the same lines to `/tmp/weather_team.txt`, in one command.

hints.text: `tee` writes what it receives to a file and passes it on to the screen at the same time.

successMessage: A `tee` in a pipeline is how you keep a record of a long job while still watching it happen.

title: Collapsing Repeats (uniq)
brief: The dome controller writes its status to `Documents/dome_status.log` every time it polls, whether or not anything changed. Show the run of readings with the repeats collapsed, so only the actual status changes are left.
objective: Print `Documents/dome_status.log` with each run of repeated lines collapsed to one.

hints.text: `uniq` drops a line that is an exact repeat of the one directly above it. Repeats that are not next to each other are left alone.

successMessage: Nine polls became three lines. `uniq` only ever compares a line to its neighbour, never to the whole file.

title: BOSS: How Many Machines Called?
brief: `Documents/server_access.log` holds one request per line, and the first field of each line is the address that made it. Several addresses appear more than once. Print how many DIFFERENT addresses appear in the file — one number, nothing else.
objective: Print how many different addresses appear in `Documents/server_access.log` — one number, nothing else.

hints.text: Four jobs on one line: take the first field of every line, put those values in order, collapse the repeats, then count what is left.

successMessage: Seven machines. Sorting before collapsing matters: duplicates are only removed when they end up next to each other.

title: Create Empty Files (touch)
brief: Open a scratch file for the night: create an empty file at `/tmp/new_file.txt`.
objective: Create an empty file at `/tmp/new_file.txt`.

hints.text: `touch` creates an empty file, or updates the timestamp of one that already exists.

successMessage: An empty file is still a file: it has a name, a size of zero, and permissions you can set.

title: Make Directories (mkdir -p)
brief: Make a new directory `projects/api`. Use the find that also creates any missing parent, so the command works whether or not `projects` is already there.
objective: Create the directory `projects/api`, creating any missing parent as well.

hints.text: `mkdir` makes directories. One find creates the missing parents and stays quiet if the directory already exists.

successMessage: `-p` is what makes a directory command safe to run twice, which is why scripts use it everywhere.

title: Copy Files (cp)
brief: Back up tonight's notes: copy `Documents/notes.txt` to `/tmp/notes_backup.txt`.
objective: Copy `Documents/notes.txt` to `/tmp/notes_backup.txt`.

hints.text: `cp` takes the source path first and the destination second.

successMessage: The original is untouched. A copy with a new name is the cheapest insurance there is.

title: Recursive Copy (cp -r)
brief: The day crew wants the whole observatory website exactly as it stands tonight — every file in it, not only the ones you happened to touch.
objective: Copy the whole `projects/web` directory, everything inside it included, to `/tmp/web_backup`.

hints.text: `cp` refuses a directory until you add the recursive find.

successMessage: All three website files came along. Recursive means "and everything underneath", however deep it goes.

title: Move & Rename (mv)
brief: The deploy script is about to be pointed at the production dome. Its name should say so before somebody runs it by accident at three in the morning.
objective: Rename `projects/scripts/deploy.py` to `deploy_prod.py`, leaving it in the same directory.

hints.text: `mv` both moves and renames: old path first, new path second. Renaming is just moving to a new name in the same place.

successMessage: There is no separate rename command on Linux, because moving a file to a new name is the same operation.

title: Remove Files (rm)
brief: `logs/debug.log` is noise and the day crew wants it gone. Delete it — and on the same line list `logs` again, so you can see for yourself that it went.
objective: Delete `logs/debug.log` and, on the same line, list `logs` to see that it went.

hints.text: `rm` removes a file. There is no undo and no recycle bin, so checking afterwards is a habit worth having.

successMessage: Two files left, and you saw it rather than assumed it. Verifying a delete costs one extra command.

title: Make Executable (chmod +x)
brief: `projects/scripts/deploy.py` cannot be run yet. Give it execute permission.
objective: Give `projects/scripts/deploy.py` execute permission.

hints.text: `chmod` also takes symbolic modes: a `+` or a `-`, then a letter for the permission.

successMessage: A script is just a text file until the execute bit is set. `+x` sets it for everybody, `u+x` only for the owner — both count here.

title: Permissions (chmod octal)
brief: Lock `Documents/notes.txt` down so the owner can read and write it and nobody else can do anything at all. Set the octal mode.
objective: Set `Documents/notes.txt` so the owner may read and write it and nobody else may do anything.

hints.text: Read is 4, write is 2, execute is 1. Add them up per column: owner, then group, then everybody else.

successMessage: Mode 600 reads as `-rw-------`: the owner, and nobody else at all.

title: Inspect Inodes & Timestamps (stat)
brief: Show the size, permissions, inode number and timestamps of `Documents/notes.txt`. A plain `ls -l` does not show all of that.
objective: Show the size, permissions, inode number and timestamps of `Documents/notes.txt`.

hints.text: One command prints a file's whole metadata block in one go.

successMessage: The inode number is the file's real identity. The name is only a label pointing at it.

title: Superuser Elevation (sudo)
brief: `/etc/shadow` holds the account password hashes and only root may read it, so `cat /etc/shadow` is refused. Read it anyway.
objective: Read `/etc/shadow`, which only root may open.

hints.text: One command runs a single other command as a different user, normally root.

successMessage: The hashes are visible, but they are hashes: readable, not reversible. That is the point of the file.
commandCheckExemptReason: Intentionally fails: the challenge teaches Permission denied and the sudo escalation that fixes it.

title: Conditional AND (&&)
brief: On one line: create the directory `/tmp/test_dir`, then create the file `/tmp/test_dir/file.txt` inside it — but only attempt the file if the directory step succeeded.
objective: In one line: create `/tmp/test_dir`, then create `/tmp/test_dir/file.txt` only if the directory step succeeded.

hints.text: One operator runs the second command only when the first one exits successfully.

successMessage: `&&` reads the exit code for you. It is how a script stops instead of ploughing on after a failure.

title: BOSS: Seal the Night's Records
brief: Before you hand over, put a copy of `logs/auth.log` into a new directory `/tmp/handover`, lock that copy so only its owner may read and write it, and list the directory in long form so the permissions are visible. One line, with the steps joined so that each runs only if the one before it worked.
objective: In one line: copy `logs/auth.log` into a new `/tmp/handover`, lock the copy to its owner, and list the directory in long form — each step only if the one before it worked.

hints.text: Four jobs on one line, chained with `&&`: make the directory, copy the file into it, change the copy's mode, then list the directory in long form.

successMessage: Make, copy, restrict, verify — and the last step proves the other three. `-rw-------` on the listing is the receipt.

title: Finding Files by Name
brief: Somewhere below your home directory there is a shell script. List every file whose name ends in `.sh`, at any depth under the directory you are in.
objective: List every file whose name ends in `.sh`, at any depth below where you are standing.

hints.text: One command walks an entire directory tree and can filter on the filename. Quote the pattern so the shell does not try to expand it first.

successMessage: One script, three levels down. Quoting the pattern hands it to `find` intact instead of letting the shell expand it in the current directory.

title: Filtering by Type
brief: List every regular file underneath `projects` — the files themselves, not the directories that hold them.
objective: List every regular file under `projects`, and no directories.

hints.text: `find` can filter by entry type. The letter for a regular file is `f`.

successMessage: Five files, no directories. Without the type filter you would get `web` and `scripts` in the list as well.

title: Stream Editing (sed)
brief: Print `Documents/data.csv` with every occurrence of `Optics` replaced by `Astrometry`. The file on disk must not change.
objective: Print `Documents/data.csv` with every `Optics` replaced by `Astrometry`, leaving the file on disk unchanged.

predicates.text:
id,name,team,hours,status
101,Alice Reyes,Astrometry,95,active
102,Bo Nakamura,Records,82,active
103,Chidi Adeyemi,Astrometry,105,active
104,Dana Ilves,Weather,115,active
105,Evan Wright,Outreach,78,inactive
106,Fiona Marsh,Weather,120,active

hints.text: `sed` edits a stream as it goes past. Its substitute script has the form s/old/new/g.

successMessage: The screen changed and the file did not. `sed` rewrites the stream on its way past, which is why it is safe to experiment with.

title: Pattern Scanning (awk)
brief: `/etc/passwd` is colon separated. Print only the username (field 1) and the home directory (field 6) for every account on this machine.
objective: Print the username and the home directory of every account in `/etc/passwd`.

predicates.text:
root /root
daemon /usr/sbin
bin /bin
sys /dev
sync /bin
student /home/student
nobody /nonexistent

hints.text: `awk` splits each line into numbered fields. One find sets the separator, and `$1` refers to the first field.

successMessage: Seven accounts, and only one of them is a person. The rest are services that own files and never log in.

title: Variable Expansion & Quotes
brief: Print the value your `HOME` variable holds. Quote it the way that still lets the shell expand it.
objective: Print the value your `HOME` variable holds, quoted so the shell still expands it.

hints.text: Double quotes still allow variable expansion. Single quotes suppress it and print the name literally.

successMessage: Double quotes expand the variable; single quotes would have printed the four characters $HOME instead.

title: Exit Codes ($?)
brief: Every program returns an exit code when it finishes: 0 means success, anything else means failure. Search `/etc/passwd` for `root`, then print the exit code that search returned — both on one line.
objective: Search `/etc/passwd` for `root`, then print the exit code that search returned — both on one line.

hints.text: `$?` holds the exit code of the command that just finished, and `;` separates two commands on one line.

successMessage: Zero means the search found something. A grep that matches nothing returns 1 — which is how scripts decide what to do next.

title: Conditional OR (||)
brief: On one line: try to read `/non_existent_file`, and if that attempt fails, print the message `File was missing`.
objective: In one line: try to read `/non_existent_file`, and print `File was missing` if the attempt fails.

hints.text: One operator runs the second command only when the first one fails.

successMessage: `||` is the fallback branch: try this, and if it does not work, do that instead.

title: Compare Files (diff)
brief: Compare `projects/web/index.html` against `projects/web/style.css` line by line, in the unified format that patch tools read.
objective: Compare `projects/web/index.html` against `projects/web/style.css` in the unified format.

hints.text: `diff` compares two files. One find selects the unified output format.

successMessage: Lines prefixed `-` are only in the first file, lines prefixed `+` only in the second. Every code review you ever read is this format.

title: Shell Mastery (history)
brief: Your handover note has to say what you actually did tonight, and the shell has been keeping that list for you the whole shift.
objective: Show every command you have typed this session.

hints.text: The shell keeps a numbered list of everything you have run. One word prints it.

successMessage: This is how you find the clever command you ran twenty minutes ago instead of reconstructing it from memory.

title: BOSS: Who Logged the Most Hours?
brief: The last thing the day crew wants before they drive up the mountain. `Documents/data.csv` lists each person's hours in column 4. Print the NAME of the person with the most hours — just the name, on its own, with nothing else around it.
objective: Print the NAME of the person with the most hours in `Documents/data.csv` — just the name, nothing else.

hints.text: Three tools on one line: put the rows in order by the hours column with the largest first, keep only the top row, then slice out the name column.

successMessage: Three tools, one line, each doing one job and handing the result to the next. That is the whole idea of the Unix shell — and it is dawn. The dome is yours.
